_meta.indication: Indicated as an adjunct to PCI to reduce the risk of periprocedural MI, repeat coronary revascularization, and stent thrombosis in patients who have not been treated with a P2Y12 platelet inhibitor and are not being given a glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor

pivotal_trials.phase: Large randomized, double-blind superiority outcome trial
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind study; patients randomized 1:1 to KENGREAL (n=5472) or to clopidogrel 300 or 600 mg (n=5470)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with coronary artery disease (stable angina, UA/NSTEMI, STEMI) requiring PCI who had not taken an oral P2Y12 inhibitor and were not receiving glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors
pivotal_trials.endpoint: First occurrence of the composite of all-cause mortality, MI, ischemia-driven revascularization (IDR), and stent thrombosis (ST) within 48 hours after randomization
pivotal_trials.n: 11,145 subjects randomized (mITT: KENGREAL N=5470, clopidogrel N=5469)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary composite endpoint: 257 (4.7%) KENGREAL vs 322 (5.9%) clopidogrel; OR 0.78 (95% CI 0.66, 0.93); p=0.005 (relative risk reduction 22%)

nct_ctgov.title: A Clinical Trial Comparing Cangrelor to Clopidogrel Standard Therapy in Subjects Who Require Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) (CHAMPION PHOENIX)

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction is bleeding; in CHAMPION PHOENIX any GUSTO bleeding (non-CABG) occurred in 857 (15.5%) with KENGREAL vs 602 (10.9%) with clopidogrel; GUSTO severe/life-threatening 11 (0.2%) vs 6 (0.1%); any TIMI bleeding 45 (0.8%) vs 17 (0.3%)
target_moa: Direct-acting P2Y12 platelet receptor inhibitor that blocks ADP-induced platelet activation and aggregation

advisory_committee.vote: Cardiovascular and Renal Advisory Committee voted 9-2 with one abstention for approval (April 15, 2015); at the first meeting (12 February 2014) the committee had voted 2 yes, 7 no, 0 abstentions on approvability for the PCI indication

summary.text: NDA 204958 (Class 2 resubmission) for cangrelor was approved on the basis of the CHAMPION PHOENIX trial after a prior Complete Response letter dated 30 April 2014; a second advisory committee voted 9-2 with one abstention for approval before full approval was granted.

citations.quote:
Application Type	NDA, Class 2 resubmission
Application Number(s)	204958
The Division issued a Complete Response (CR) letter to the Applicant on 30 April 2014 identifying the reasons for not approving cangrelor at that time.
This application was discussed for a second time by the Cardiovascular and Renal Advisory Committee on April 15 2015. The Committee voted 9-2 with one abstention for approval.

basis.text: Issues leading to the CRL included that some subcomponents of the primary endpoint in CHAMPION PHOENIX may not represent clinical benefit, relevancy of CHAMPION PHOENIX data to current American practice, and general approvability

citations.quote: The issues raised during the review process and during the AC meeting leading to a complete response letter are listed here:

- Some subcomponents of the primary endpoint in CHAMPION PHOENIX may not represent clinical benefit
- Relevancy of CHAMPION PHOENIX data to current American practice
- General approvability
- Transition from cangrelor to an oral P2Y12 antagonist
- Uncertainty about cangrelor utility in patients with stable angina undergoing PCI
- Baseline clinical diagnosis: “derived patient type” vs. investigator
